audience: Laboratory operations and digital project sponsors
constraints: Confirm instrument interface, data path, quality requirements, access, and validation expectations before pilot selection.
tagline: Test one instrument. Trace one data path.
idea_summary: Explore connecting one laboratory instrument to the electronic recording environment to test an end-to-end data path for a QC1 characterization workflow.
problem_statement: Instrument results may require manual saving, moving, scanning, transcription, or review. Which steps occur in the target workflow and what controls apply still need confirmation.

steps: Manual handling may occur before electronic recording or review
pain_points: Manual handling may occur; the target workflow and extent require confirmation

steps: Trace the result through one controlled end-to-end data path
Review the resulting workflow with relevant stakeholders
changes: Evaluate a bounded connection rather than assume an integration exists

value_proposition: A small, instrument-specific pilot could help stakeholders assess a proposed electronic data path before making a broader commitment.

benefits.statement: The pilot could provide evidence about workflow fit, data traceability, and review needs.

success_measures.measure: End-to-end data path can be demonstrated for the selected workflow
success_measures.basis: Proposed pilot criterion; threshold to be agreed

success_measures.measure: Relevant quality, security, and data-governance questions are documented
success_measures.basis: Proposed pilot criterion; owners to be agreed

dependencies: Instrument interface and access need assessment
Quality, security, privacy, and data-governance review needs identification

risks.statement: The required instrument interface or data path may not be available
risks.mitigation: Confirm interface and access with system owners before pilot commitment

risks.statement: Quality, validation, security, or data-integrity expectations may change pilot scope
risks.mitigation: Identify appropriate reviewers and applicable requirements before testing

assumptions: A candidate instrument and workflow can be selected for discovery; availability is not confirmed.
unknowns: Which instrument, model, and workflow should be selected?
Which electronic recording environment and interface are in scope?
What quality, validation, security, and data-integrity requirements apply?
Who is the sponsor and who can authorize a pilot?
What baseline and thresholds would make the pilot useful?

options.name: Continue discovery
options.description: Confirm workflow, owners, interfaces, requirements, and a measurable pilot boundary.

options.name: Defer the concept
options.description: Pause until a sponsor, workflow, and technical path can be confirmed.

recommended_option: Continue discovery before any pilot commitment.
recommended_next_step: Run a short discovery with laboratory, quality, IT, and data-governance stakeholders to select one instrument and workflow, verify interface options, and agree pilot acceptance criteria.
pilot_definition: If discovery supports it, propose a bounded pilot using one instrument, one QC1 characterization workflow, and one end-to-end data path. Confirm authorization, quality requirements, access, and success criteria before execution.

brand_brief.tagline: Test one instrument. Trace one data path.
brand_brief.typography: System sans-serif; strong readable headings; no corporate marks
brand_brief.logo_rationale: A simple, independent path-and-point motif suggests a traceable data journey without implying an approved product or corporate affiliation.
brand_brief.accessibility: Use high-contrast text, labels in addition to color, and a recognizable silhouette at small sizes.
